title: Round 27 Ohio-Pennsylvania state-frame USGS GNIS source register
scope: All-GNIS starter registers for Ohio and Pennsylvania. Every seeded row reproduces one USGS GNIS record screened by exact official name, returned type/state/county, permanent FEATURE_ID, and returned GNIS primary point, and cross-checked on two independent USGS surfaces (USGS GNIS Geocoder; staged-products DomesticNames text via tools/gnis_extract.py; cumulative candidate extract resources/city-subsurface/gnis-candidates-batch7.json with per-state ZIP SHA-256 values). Campbell Hill and Mount Davis additionally carry Domestic Names per-ID identity checks. The Indian Lake coordinate anomaly is recorded as a known service discrepancy.

usgsGeocoder.use: Fuzzy candidate discovery only. A candidate was accepted only when Name, Type, State, County, GnisId, Latitude, and Longitude all matched the intended feature and the point lay inside the intended state. Counties, census divisions, pools, canals, historical places, and same-name records of another class or county were rejected explicitly where relevant.

gnisDomesticNames.use: Second-surface cross-check of every seeded FEATURE_ID and per-ID identity checks for Campbell Hill (1079572) and Mount Davis (1209050), extracted in a GitHub Actions runner by tools/gnis_extract.py. The current text layout carries no elevation columns, so the two high-point elevations cite USGS-published state-highpoint values. The candidate extract file is cumulative across batches 7-10; this register is the frozen batch-10 evidence.

selectionRules: VERIFIED=1 is claimed only for an exact official name, compatible GNIS feature class/type, intended state and returned primary county, permanent FEATURE_ID, and an official point returned by a cited USGS service, reproduced identically on the second USGS surface.

A row is additionally rejected when the agreed GNIS point itself is geographically impossible for the named feature (see the Indian Lake discrepancy); two-surface agreement is necessary but not sufficient evidence.

Grouped Geocoder Types map explicitly to stored row classes: Cities & Populated Places to Populated Place, Lakes & Reservoirs to Lake for the accepted named lakes and reservoirs, Streams & Canals to Stream for the accepted river records, and Summit to Summit.
A stored GNIS primary point is never described as a municipal boundary, street-address geocode, generic centroid, shoreline polygon, summit outline, or river centerline.

If exact-name candidates remain indistinguishable, or the state-filtered screen returns no intended feature record, the feature is omitted from that state gazetteer and may appear only as a generalized context corridor.
Statewide frames use explicitly synthetic relief gaussians and generalized corridors; no bundled DEM or surveyed boundary is implied.

ohio.title: Ohio statewide frame (Ohio-Pennsylvania batch)
ohio.frameNote: Ohio-Pennsylvania batch: the Columbus capital anchor is balanced with the per-ID Campbell Hill high point, the Grand Lake reservoir, three in-state river-mouth records (Scioto, Maumee, Cuyahoga), and a seeded Lake Erie GNIS anchor in Ohio waters. The Ohio main stem remains a corridor after its fourth consecutive empty state screen (IL, IN, OH, PA). Indian Lake is excluded: both USGS surfaces agree on a longitude that falls in Pennsylvania (see identityDecisions).

identityDecisions.candidate: Campbell Hill, FEATURE_ID 1048578 (Pike County) and 1038781 (Scioto County)
identityDecisions.decision: Rejected. Three Ohio summits share the name; the seeded Logan County record 1079572 matches the published Ohio high-point location near Bellefontaine, and the DomesticNames_OH_Text extract reproduces all three records at distinct points.
identityDecisions.notClaimed: The seeded point is not a surveyed summit outline.

identityDecisions.decision: Not seeded. The Geocoder returned the Logan County lake at longitude -80.8753645, a point in western Pennsylvania roughly 275 km east of the Logan County reservoir (which lies near -83.88), and the DomesticNames_OH_Text extract reproduces the identical longitude, so the error is in the GNIS record itself rather than in either delivery surface. A Pennsylvania point cannot be stored in the Ohio frame; the feature is excluded pending a GNIS correction.
identityDecisions.knownServiceDiscrepancy: GNIS FEATURE_ID 1041943 carries a corrupted longitude on both USGS surfaces (Geocoder service and staged-products text agree exactly); county (Logan) and latitude are consistent with the true reservoir location. Recorded here rather than silently normalized; no coordinate was hand-corrected.
identityDecisions.notClaimed: No replacement point was estimated or stored for Indian Lake.

identityDecisions.decision: Empty screens, completing a four-state pattern (IL, IN, OH, PA all empty): the single main-stem record returns under another state's association. No row seeded in either frame; it remains a generalized context corridor in both.
identityDecisions.notClaimed: The corridors are not channel centerlines or state boundaries.

identityDecisions.decision: Not seeded. The Geocoder returned two Lakes & Reservoirs records for the same border reservoir in the same county (1044806 and 1199940) at points about 4 km apart; 1044806 is seeded, following the Lake of the Woods multipoint precedent (round 24).
identityDecisions.knownServiceDiscrepancy: Two permanent FEATURE_IDs describe one intended reservoir (multipoint duplication); the register preserves the accepted record and names the unseeded duplicate.
identityDecisions.notClaimed: The seeded point is not a shoreline or the state-line segment of the reservoir.

identityDecisions.decision: Rejected. Same-name communities at the opposite ends of the state; the seeded records are the Dauphin County capital (1213649) and the Lehigh County city (1213700).

identityDecisions.candidate: Susquehanna River and Delaware River under states=PA; Lake Erie under states=PA
identityDecisions.decision: Empty screens. The Susquehanna record's primary point is the Maryland Chesapeake mouth and the Delaware record's is the Delaware Bay mouth; both rivers remain corridors. Lake Erie's single GNIS record returns under states=OH and is seeded once there (FEATURE_ID 1075813); Erie's city record anchors the Pennsylvania shore.
identityDecisions.notClaimed: The corridors are not channel centerlines, shorelines, or state boundaries.

identityDecisions.candidate: Youngstown and Canton (Ohio); Reading and Bethlehem (Pennsylvania)
identityDecisions.decision: Identity-safe candidates in the batch-10 extract, omitted under the starter-scope treatment; the 12-row starters keep the capital anchors plus statewide coverage.
identityDecisions.notClaimed: Starter-scope omission is not a claim about feature importance or identity.

knownLimitations: Ohio and Pennsylvania are starter registers, not statewide GNIS extracts. Each contains 12 deliberately selected identity-safe rows.

The USGS Geocoder is a suggestion service; exact-match screening by name/type/state/county/FEATURE_ID is part of the evidence. Every seeded row was reproduced on the second USGS surface (staged-products DomesticNames text) at the same primary point; the Indian Lake decision records the one case where both surfaces share a source-level error, and the feature was excluded rather than hand-corrected.

The current DomesticNames text layout carries no elevation columns, so Campbell Hill (1,550 feet) and Mount Davis (3,213 feet) elevations cite USGS-published state-highpoint values; GNIS identity for both rests on the per-ID class/county/point reproduction.

GNIS point data do not supply the displayed terrain or corridors. Both frames use explicitly synthetic relief gaussians and generalized context lines; the Lake Erie row stores a mid-lake reference point and draws no shoreline.
State frames are rectangles, not state-boundary clipping masks. Both rectangles include areas outside their state outlines (including Canadian waters of Lake Erie); no boundary geometry is claimed.
